ledger.what: remove cookie/consent chrome (OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, generic cookie-banner ids/classes, any cookie/consent/gdpr-named element inside a fixed/sticky/high-z overlay)
ledger.why: overlay chrome injected by a CMP, not page content; re-added at deploy time

ledger.what: de-carousel slick/swiper/splide/glide: remove clone slides, force real slides visible+static, drop dots/arrows
ledger.why: hidden slides are absent from innerText and clones duplicate it — rotating carousels break byte determinism; the reskin renders all slides statically in DOM order
UI chrome injected by the source theme, no content bytes; donor kit has its own Back to Top module

ledger.what: expand every main .nsw-accordion: drop hidden="until-found" from .nsw-accordion__content and set the button aria-expanded="true"
ledger.why: collapsed panels are authored content absent from innerText (hidden); without expansion the byte reference silently drops every accordion body. Same rule as the default de-carousel (N-D2): interactive disclosure is normalized to all-open, and the reskin renders each item title followed by its panel statically in DOM order

visibleTextNormalized: Our principal and staff Welcome from our principal It is my honour to be Principal at Fort Street High School. It goes without saying that it is also an incredible responsibility to lead a school with such a history in nurturing and producing so many great Australians. Fort Street High School is a co-educational, academically selective, public high school with a long and proud history. Established in 1849 as a Model school, it is the oldest government high school in Australia. All students at Fort Street are encouraged to reach their full potential and enjoy a dynamic and rich school experience. The school fosters an environment where intelligent young men and women can express both their individuality and develop a strong sense of belonging and a commitment to social justice. Fort Street High School offers a broad curriculum and an extensive range of co-curricular programs to challenge and inspire all students. We have a strong focus on student leadership, on promoting positive values and developing a sense of global citizenship. The school community truly represents multicultural Australia, and is a harmonious community which respects each individual. Students come from 100 suburbs of Sydney. Our students speak about 40 different languages and enrich the life of this great school, a school which is known for tolerance and acceptance. It is my privilege to work with the wider community, parents, P&C, the Fort Street Foundation, the School Council and the Fortians Union to maintain the important traditions and ensure that the school is a leader in education in the twenty first century. Our alumni continue a deep connection with our community and have extensive involvement in the life of the school which is evidence of their rich and significant educational journey and the Fortian pride that has been fostered. Ms Juliette McMurray, Principal of Fort Street High School School Staff for 2025 Teachers at Fort Street are committed to helping our gifted students reach their academic potential by creating programs which build on the learning continuum, promote creative and critical thinking and incorporate differentiation to give them challenging and meaningful learning experiences. Our staff come from a wide range of backgrounds themselves, and bringing a diverse range of talents and skills, teachers celebrate the diversity found in the classroom. Senior Executive Our school leaders, including our principal, guide teachers and students. They help create a school culture where every child is supported to grow and thrive. Our teachers bring experience, care and a passion for learning to every lesson. With a focus on success, they help every child reach their full potential.
